title: How To Be Free Of School Drama And Politics
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that a single deliberate choice can insulate a teacher entirely from school politics, gossip, and drama: letting go of ego, reputation, and any concern for what colleagues think. He describes the minority of colleagues who thrive on tension and scheming and how they pull everyone else into watching their back, calculating words, and building alliances just to survive the social environment. His proposed alternative is a list of specific behavioral guidelines — keeping professional distance, never taking criticism personally, treating everyone with equal kindness, staying humble and busy, keeping secrets, and putting yourself last — that together amount to stepping outside the status competition entirely. He frames the paradox at the center of the piece as the payoff: teachers who stop chasing reputation and status end up earning genuine respect and are left alone, above the fray, precisely because they've stopped needing anything from anyone.
points: A single deliberate choice — jettisoning ego, reputation, and concern for others' opinions — can insulate a teacher from school politics and drama entirely.
Colleagues who thrive on tension and scheming pull everyone else into watching their back and calculating their words just to survive socially.
Specific guidelines for staying above the fray include: never take criticism personally, treat everyone with equal kindness, don't try to look good, and keep secrets.
The central paradox: teachers who stop chasing reputation and status end up earning the deepest respect, precisely because they need nothing from anyone.
Maintaining pleasantness and politeness while standing apart from the 'scrum' is what lets a teacher avoid ever being dragged into office politics.
quotes: There is a choice you can make today that will insulate you from all school-related drama and politics.
You have to watch your back, build alliances, and defend your record. You have to calculate the words you use or hold your tongue or work the angles.
It’s to jettison your ego, your reputation, and your concern about what anyone ever thinks about you. It’s to not allow any attachment. No string. No scent. No vapor leaking into the maelstrom.
As long as you maintain your pleasantness and politeness, you need never to get dragged in.
Funny thing, though: The last shall be first. The egoless becomes the leader. Seeking no reputation builds reputation.
The one who doesn’t boast or climb or need is set apart, held up, untouchable and left alone to remain above the boiling stew.
